text: Students must register for courses during the designated registration period each semester.
Late registration requires approval from the academic dean and may incur additional fees.
Course registration is finalized once payment of tuition and fees is confirmed by the bursar.
Students are responsible for verifying their course schedule accuracy before the add-drop deadline.
Web registration is available to all students with no outstanding financial or academic holds.
First-year students must meet with their academic advisor before registering for courses.
Registration priority is determined by class standing and cumulative grade point average.
Students may not register for more than 20 credit hours in a single semester without special permission.
Waitlisted courses will be automatically added if space becomes available during registration. Additional details are available in the student handbook.
Cross-registration with partner institutions requires prior approval from both registrars.
The add-drop period extends through the second week of the semester for standard courses.
Students may add courses without penalty during the first week of the semester.
Dropping a course after the add-drop deadline results in a withdrawal notation on the transcript. Policies are subject to change by faculty vote.
Courses dropped during the add-drop period do not appear on the official academic transcript.
Students must maintain a minimum of 12 credit hours after the add-drop period to remain full-time. Questions should be directed to the appropriate administrative office.
Laboratory and studio courses may have earlier add-drop deadlines than lecture courses.
The university employs a four-point grading scale with plus and minus designations.
A grade of incomplete may be assigned when a student has satisfactorily completed most coursework.
Incomplete grades must be resolved within six weeks of the following semester.
Pass-fail grading is available for elective courses outside the student's major department.
Grade appeals must be submitted in writing to the department chair within thirty days.
The grade point average is calculated by dividing quality points by attempted credit hours.
Repeated courses replace the previous grade in the cumulative grade point average calculation. Policies are subject to change by faculty vote.
All students must complete the general education curriculum regardless of major.
The general education program includes coursework in arts, humanities, natural sciences, and social sciences.
Students must demonstrate quantitative reasoning competency through approved mathematics courses.
Global citizenship requirements may be satisfied through study away or designated domestic programs.
First-year seminars introduce students to academic inquiry and university resources.
Writing and communication requirements ensure proficiency in academic and professional discourse.
General education courses may not be taken pass-fail except under extraordinary circumstances.
Each major requires a minimum of ten courses at the 200-level or above.
Major declarations are due by the end of the fourth semester of enrollment.
Students must maintain a minimum grade point average of 2.0 in major coursework.
Capstone projects integrate knowledge and skills acquired throughout the major curriculum.
Independent study courses may count toward the major with departmental approval.
Double majors require completion of all requirements for both programs without course overlap.
Interdisciplinary majors combine coursework from multiple departments under a unified theme.
Candidates for graduation must file a degree application by the deadline published by the registrar.
All degree requirements must be completed by the date of commencement exercises. Additional details are available in the student handbook.
Students with outstanding incomplete grades are not eligible to graduate.
Diplomas are mailed to the permanent address on file approximately eight weeks after graduation. See the registrar website for current deadlines and forms.
Latin honors are awarded based on the cumulative grade point average at the time of graduation.
Commencement participation is permitted for students completing requirements in the subsequent summer term.
All students are bound by the university honor code from matriculation through graduation. Questions should be directed to the appropriate administrative office.
The honor code prohibits plagiarism, cheating, fabrication, and unauthorized collaboration. See the registrar website for current deadlines and forms.
Students must sign the honor pledge on all examinations and major assignments.
Violations of the honor code are reported to the student judicial board for review. Questions should be directed to the appropriate administrative office.
The honor code applies to all academic work including laboratory reports and creative projects.
Ignorance of citation standards does not excuse plagiarism under the honor code.
Academic integrity violations may result in sanctions ranging from warning to expulsion.
First-time offenders in minor cases may receive a reduced grade and mandatory ethics workshop.
Repeated violations or egregious misconduct may result in suspension or permanent dismissal.
The student judicial board considers intent, severity, and prior record when determining sanctions.
Appeals of academic integrity sanctions must be filed within ten business days of notification.
Study away programs are available at partner institutions on six continents.
Students may study away for one semester or a full academic year.
All study away coursework must be pre-approved by the academic advisor and registrar.
Credits earned through approved study away programs transfer as graded credit toward the degree. Questions should be directed to the appropriate administrative office.
Financial aid may be applied to approved study away programs with prior authorization.
Students must be in good academic standing to be eligible for study away opportunities. Additional details are available in the student handbook.
Application deadlines for study away programs are typically one year before departure.
Transfer credits from study away programs require official transcripts from the host institution.
A maximum of sixteen transfer credits may be applied toward degree requirements.
Transfer credits must be earned at accredited institutions with comparable academic standards.
Courses taken pass-fail at other institutions generally do not transfer for degree credit.
The registrar evaluates transfer credits for equivalency to university courses.
Each student is assigned a faculty advisor upon declaration of major.
Academic advisors assist with course selection, degree planning, and career preparation.
Students may request a change of advisor by submitting a petition to the dean.
Pre-professional advisors provide guidance for students pursuing graduate or professional school.
Peer advisors are available during orientation and registration periods.
The university provides comprehensive mental health counseling services to all enrolled students. Policies are subject to change by faculty vote.
Wellness workshops address stress management, sleep hygiene, and mindfulness practices.
Disability support services ensure equitable access to academic programs and facilities.
Students may request accommodations by registering with the disability services office.
Emergency mental health support is available twenty-four hours through the counseling hotline.
The career center offers resume review, interview preparation, and job search strategy sessions.
On-campus recruiting events connect students with employers from diverse industries. See the registrar website for current deadlines and forms.
Internship funding is available for students pursuing unpaid summer experiences. Questions should be directed to the appropriate administrative office.
Alumni mentorship programs pair current students with graduates in related fields.
Career assessment tools help students identify strengths and potential career pathways.
Annual tuition is set by the board of trustees and published on the bursar website.
Tuition payments are due in full before the start of each semester.
Payment plans are available for families preferring to spread costs across monthly installments. Policies are subject to change by faculty vote.
Late payment penalties accrue at a rate specified in the student financial agreement.
Tuition refunds follow a sliding scale based on the date of official withdrawal.
Need-based financial aid is determined by the institutional methodology assessment. See the registrar website for current deadlines and forms.
Merit scholarships are awarded at admission and renewed based on academic performance. Policies are subject to change by faculty vote.
Students receiving financial aid must maintain satisfactory academic progress.
Financial aid packages may include grants, loans, and work-study employment.
Appeals for additional aid require documentation of changed financial circumstances.
International students are eligible for merit-based and select need-based aid programs.
All first-year and second-year students are required to live in university housing.
Residential life staff provide programming and support for campus communities.
Housing assignments are made by the housing office based on preference forms and availability.
Room changes are permitted during designated periods with approval from residential life.
Recognized student organizations receive funding and administrative support from student affairs. Policies are subject to change by faculty vote.
New organizations may apply for recognition by submitting a constitution and faculty sponsor. See the registrar website for current deadlines and forms.
Student government represents undergraduate interests to the administration and faculty.
Registration holds related to academic integrity violations must be cleared before course enrollment is permitted.
Students completing study away requirements in their final semester must submit transcripts before graduation clearance.
Academic advisors work closely with the financial aid office to ensure students understand aid implications of course load changes.
Transfer credits from study away may satisfy general education requirements with approval from the curriculum committee.
The honor code applies to all academic work completed at the university, including courses taken during study away programs.
Merit scholarship recipients who violate the honor code may face review of their financial aid standing by the scholarship committee.
Residential life staff coordinate with student support services to provide wellness programming in campus housing.
Capstone courses may involve collaboration with community partners, subject to the same academic integrity standards as traditional coursework.
